title: What If You Could See Everyone's Real-Life Rating?
description:
One morning, a player rating card appears above everyone's head. And it's always right.

Mine says 41. The captain everyone worships is a 71. And the kid who gets picked last every single time? He's a 94!

So I build a team out of everyone the school ignored, and bet everything on Saturday's cup. Then we lose 6–0, and I find out the rating doesn't measure everything. 

What would YOUR rating be? Tell me in the comments 👇


#WhatIf #Animation #Football #Storytime

title: What If You Could See Everyone's Real-Life Rating? Part2
description:
What if you could see everyone's real-life rating floating above their head? I used it to build a team to win the cup.

One morning, a player rating card appears above everyone's head. And it's always right.

Part one: https://youtu.be/kS222TGe8Nc

Every kid at the City Academy trial is a ninety, while my own rating is just forty-two. After discovering I could see the hidden stats of every player around me, I decided to recruit the kids the school ignored. This animated story follows my attempt to prove that numbers do not tell the whole truth about football talent.

We bet everything on Saturday's big game, but losing six-nil taught me that potential is not always what it seems. I learned the hard way that a player card cannot measure heart or determination on the pitch.

If you were given the ability to see these ratings, who is the first person you would check? Tell me in the comments, and subscribe for new animated stories every week.

title: What If You Could See How Everyone Rates You 1 to 10?
description:
You walk into school thinking you're a solid seven. Then you look closer. Above every head in the hallway there's a number: how that person rates you, right now, out of ten. Two. One and a half. Three. And under every number, a list of tips for how to become a ten.

What if you could see how everyone rates you? By lunch, the queen of the school is chasing you down the hallway. A lunch lady tries to give you her car. A physics teacher gives you an A-plus for one movie quote. By Saturday, a billionaire hands you a million dollars. Then one night, at his party, you meet a man whose number goes below zero, and his list of tips says only: ERROR. NO ACTION AVAILABLE.

What would your number be, and would you even want to know? Tell us in the comments.

Subscribe to DOOMPERK for more animated What If stories.

This is a fictional What If story. The facts in it are real:
- In experiments, people form a first impression of a face (how trustworthy or likable it looks) after seeing it for about a tenth of a second, and a longer look barely changes it (Willis & Todorov, 2006).
- In "Back to the Future" (1985), Doc Brown says the time machine needs 1.21 gigawatts.
- The numbers over people's heads, Ridgemont High, Thorne Dynamics and every character are made up for the story.

title: What If You Could See Everyone's IQ?
description:
What if you could see everyone's IQ floating above their heads? 🧠👀

Imagine having a genius-level IQ of 160 but still failing your exams, while the smartest-looking student in class gets straight A's with only 70 IQ. 💀

But when the two compete to prove who's actually smarter, things take an unexpected turn.

Does having a higher IQ really make you smarter, or is there more to intelligence than just a number? 🤔

title: What If You Could See Everyone’s Lie Count?
description:
Above every face you look at, a red number: every lie that person has ever told. You're the only one who can see it.
You're a brand-new judge, proud you could always spot a liar. Nine days with the real thing change everything.

She's at the door, and you can see the number. Do you ask the questions, or say nothing and keep the life you had? Tell us which in the comments.

title: What If You Could See How Long Everyone Has Left?
description:
What if a timer floated above every person you met, showing exactly how long they had left: days, hours, minutes, seconds?

You’re Sam, 19. You fix bikes, you live with your family, and you’re the only person on Earth who can see the numbers. Green means decades. Orange means years. Red means hurry. You’ve quietly saved 31 strangers who will never know your name.

Then one Thursday morning, your little sister’s number drops from 81 years to 2 days.

You have 48 hours. Nobody believes you. And every fix you try moves the number, but none of them make it go away.

Can you change the future when you can see everyone’s ending except your own?

title: What If You Could See Everyone's Rank?
description:
What if you could see exactly where EVERYONE ranks in real life? 👀

Imagine walking into school and discovering a glowing number above every person's head.

#1 — The most respected.
#34 — Climbing fast.
#612 — The very bottom.

And suddenly, everyone knows exactly where they stand.

But what happens when your rank starts rising... while your best friend's number keeps falling?

🏆 **WELCOME TO A WORLD WHERE EVERYONE HAS A RANK.**

At first, it seems like the ultimate ability.

You can see who's on top, who's losing popularity, and who's secretly falling behind.

Your rank jumps from #487 to #34.

People start noticing you. New friendships appear. Everyone wants to be close to you.

But your best friend Max is disappearing from the spotlight.

His rank drops to #612.

And the closer you get to #1, the more you realize something is terribly wrong.

Then a mysterious rule appears.

**RULE #4: ???**

What if becoming the most important person in school meant losing the one person who truly cared about you?

💔 **IS BEING #1 WORTH LOSING YOUR BEST FRIEND?**

In this original RealityX animated story, a mysterious ranking system changes everything about friendship, popularity, loyalty, and social status.

title: What If You Could See Your Rank in Everyone’s Life?
description:
🥇 What if you could see exactly where you rank in everyone’s life? Your sister puts you third. Then a woman you’ve never met appears with a glowing #1 above her head. Somehow, you matter most to a complete stranger.

👀 Pastries, favors, fixing things—you try everything to climb the rankings. But the harder you chase first place, the easier it becomes to miss what people actually need from you.

🛠️ Between a neighbor’s moving boxes, a cookie tin full of screws, and a school play with one very wobbly moon, being important to someone turns out to be more complicated than a number. 🍪🌙

💬 What would hurt more: discovering you aren’t someone’s number one, or watching them grow happier while your rank goes down?
